clue.text: Carved bust of a nominal leader

definitions.meaning: a carved bust or figure fixed to the prow of an old sailing ship
a person who is head in name only, with no real power

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the ornamental carving on a ship's bow; the other is a leader who holds a title but no real authority.

clue.text: Thief's unusual obsession

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the word before it are set out in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: A burglar has a strange compulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges all six letters of THIEFS, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation or compulsive preoccupation with something is a synonym.

clue.text: Left you in France to return information about protein found in grains

indicators.note: about tells us the information word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: to return tells us the French word is read backwards in a down light

parts.note: tu is the familiar French word for you

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a French friend to go back with facts about a cereal protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gen' is British slang for information, and 'tu' is the familiar French 'you', so 'to return' reverses it before 'about' wraps everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the elastic protein in wheat, barley and rye that coeliacs must avoid.

clue.text: Come into social contact as one might do in a crowded room

definitions.meaning: to mix socially with other people, especially those of higher status

definitions.text: one might do in a crowded room
definitions.meaning: the literal sense: physically brushing upper arms against other people in a crush

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mingling with others, and taken literally describes bodies jostling shoulder to shoulder in a packed space.

clue.text: Kick the shins of a poor horse

definitions.meaning: in football or rugby, to kick an opponent on the leg
an old or worn-out horse kept for ordinary riding

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is fouling a player by kicking at the legs; the noun sense is a tired nag hired out for riding.

clue.text: Ted's action interrupted the story-teller

indicators.note: interrupted suggests the letters of the two words before it are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ted's activity cut short someone telling a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted' scrambles TEDS plus ACTION into the ten letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur who relates short amusing tales is one who tells stories.

clue.text: Scarlet duck going back to the water

indicators.note: going back tells us the combined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A bright red duck waddles back towards a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns REDO into the river's name; 'duck' is cricket's zero score, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a body of water; this one flows along the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Cheat a servile dependant to get control

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating or swindling them
a minion is a fawning follower or underling

explanation.surface: To gain power, someone swindles a fawning underling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereignty or authority over territory or people.

clue.text: Stranger residing in one of the best seats

indicators.note: read as 'more strange', it says the next word's letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: An outsider is living in a top seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for a person but is the anagram signal on RESIDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats beside a boxing ring are prized as the closest view of the action.

clue.text: Awkwardly handles sailors instrument of torture

parts.note: to thumb something is to handle it clumsily, as with fumbling fingers
the crew of a ship are its sailors

explanation.surface: A clumsy person fumbles with a torturer's device belonging to seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkwardly' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the synonym: thumbs means handles clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval device for crushing the fingers was used to extract confessions.

clue.text: Last word in the services

parts.note: the services are church services, and the closing word of a prayer or hymn is the one meant, not the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew affirmation 'so be it' closes prayers and hymns in church worship.

clue.text: Picture includes note with two last letters replacing net on fraud

indicators.note: includes tells us the outer string holds the note and the letters inside it
in a down clue, on means the rearranged letters sit after the picture word

parts.note: an emblem is a symbolic picture or device

indicators.note: replacing tells us the letters of net are put back in a different place

parts.note: E is a musical note
Z is the last letter of the alphabet, so two of them

explanation.surface: An image depicts a musical note while a net is moved in a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'two last letters' are the alphabet's final letter twice; 'replacing' is an anagram signal on net, and 'on' places that after the picture in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Misappropriating funds entrusted to one's care is a form of financial deceit.

clue.text: Spot the boil

parts.note: to spot something is to see it

explanation.surface: Notice a boil on someone's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boil' looks like a noun for a skin swelling, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bubble and churn like liquid at high heat; also to fume with anger.

clue.text: Scraps from additional fellows way back

parts.note: odd can mean extra or additional, as in an odd one
men are fellows

indicators.note: back tells us the abbreviation for a road or way is read backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Leftovers come from some extra blokes on a road going back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ST into TS at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd remnants and leftover bits are scraps.

clue.text: Recording a different slip of alterations to be made

definitions.text: slip of alterations to be made

indicators.note: different says the letters of the words before it come out in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A recording is changed on a list of edits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges RECORDINGA; the definition is a printed list of errors in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An errata sheet inserted in a book lists mistakes to be corrected.

clue.text: Not in danger in a clearing?

definitions.meaning: safe, having come through the difficult stage
literally, having left the trees and stepped into open ground

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being safe after trouble; literally it describes someone who has emerged from the trees into a clearing.

clue.text: Alone I criticised-there's nothing in it

indicators.note: in it tells us the zero goes inside the word for criticised

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lonely person says I was attacked, and there's no truth in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in it' puts O inside SLATED after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set apart from others, cut off and solitary.

clue.text: Saved gals Dave abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained letters thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The rescued women were left by Dave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges GALS plus DAVE; the eight letters need the S of 'gals', lost in transcription.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescued, especially goods recovered from a wreck or disaster.

clue.text: Usual dimensions of a flag perhaps

definitions.meaning: the normal, regular measurements of something
a standard is a flag, so this is how big a flag is

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means normal measurements, and punningly the bigness of a banner.

clue.text: How a bride, starting from the top, might undress

definitions.text: How a bride, starting from the top, might undress

parts.words: How a bride, starting from the top, might undress
parts.note: the first thing a bride removes from her head is the face covering she wears up the aisle, a word meaning to reveal

explanation.definitionFit: To reveal by taking off a covering, as a bride lifts the lace over her face.

clue.text: Against a Nicaraguan rebel

definitions.meaning: the Latin preposition meaning opposed to
a member of the US-backed guerrilla force opposing the Sandinistas in the 1980s

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for opposing is also the name of the 1980s Nicaraguan insurgents.

clue.text: Means of influencing the power of the bar

definitions.meaning: power to sway people or outcomes
the mechanical advantage gained by using a bar as a lever

explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively it is clout; literally it is the force multiplied by a crowbar pivoting on a fulcrum.

clue.text: The continental worker has nothing by the shed

parts.note: le is the French for the
an ant is a worker insect
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A French labourer has nothing except a garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shelter or outbuilding propped against a wall.

clue.text: Girl to leave 22 upset

indicators.note: upset means the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
leave tells us the word to is taken out of the other answer

parts.note: the answer to 22 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is upset to have to leave a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' removes TO from LEANTO, leaving LEAN; 'upset' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Lena is a female first name.

clue.text: Set off in direction of first country

indicators.note: first tells us the direction word comes before the other piece

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of
to go is to set off or depart

explanation.surface: Leave, heading for the first nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is a placement word, not the definition: the direction word stands ahead of the departure word.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic in West Africa between Ghana and Benin.

clue.text: Stake found by hollow containing engineers earlier

indicators.note: containing tells us the stake and hollow words enclose the engineers

parts.note: the ante is the stake put into the pot in poker
a dent is a hollow
CE stands for Civil Engineers

explanation.surface: A post is found in a hole holding engineers who were there before.
explanation.walkthrough: Solvers expect RE for engineers; here it is Civil Engineers, and 'containing' means the stake and hollow together surround them.
explanation.definitionFit: Antecedent describes something that came before, prior or preceding.

clue.text: The same again and again for an old bird

indicators.note: again and again tells us the word for the same is written twice

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same

explanation.surface: Repetition suits a stale old fowl.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the ditto abbreviation used in lists for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius died out in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Volunteers hurried to inform one of the dance

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
ran means hurried
to tell is to inform
a means one

explanation.surface: Reservists rushed to report one of the dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer military reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling Italian folk dance in fast six-eight time.
